subject.title: Exploring a chat-first Android surface for OpenClaw (discussion + possible focused upstreaming)

question: Should the official Android app move toward a chat-first default or mode, accept focused UX/media/connectivity PR slices while keeping Overview-first, or keep chat-first Android forks external for now?
rationale: Current main and the latest release partially address chat access, but changing the default surface or broader media/connectivity scope affects onboarding, pairing, permissions, release posture, and Android product direction.

options.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
options.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation PRs.

options.title: Keep Overview-first for now
options.body: Document that the official app remains an Overview-first companion node and ask contributors to file only specific defects or small UX improvements.

options.title: Sponsor a chat-first mode
options.body: Have maintainers explicitly sponsor a chat-first default or mode and require upgrade, onboarding, permission, and media proof before merge.

recommendation.title: Scope focused Android PR slices
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while Android owners define narrow launch/navigation, media, and connectivity slices with real-device proof before accepting implementation PRs.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision is primarily Android app product scope, and @obviyus is the named Android app owner with relevant chat-routing history.
